newsitem.title: USA: Zaire refugee movement puzzles U.S. officials.
newsitem.headline: Zaire refugee movement puzzles U.S. officials.

text.p: The apparent movement of thousands of Rwandan refugees toward home from eastern Zaire was an "interesting development" but not enough was known to understand its significance, a U.S. official said on Friday.
"It's an interesting development. Is it a key development? We don't know yet. It's hard to say what it portends," said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Whether the movement of refugees toward home was "tactical. It's hard to say," the U.S. official said, adding: "We're trying to find all this out ... We have nothing more" than has been reported on wire services.
At the White House, spokesman David Johnson called the refugee movement a "hopeful sign" but did not elaborate.

In Zaire, Ray Wilkinson of the U.N. refugee agency told Reuters: "We have between 300,000 and 400,000 people on the move ... This is a very rough estimate. We got within five km (three miles) of the village of Sake which is around 20 km (12 miles) west of Mugunga. From this point back to Goma the road is completely blocked with moving refugees."

The United States this week tentatively agreed to send 1,000 troops to Goma, Zaire to secure the airport and set up a protected corridor so refugees can return to Rwanda if they want to. Another 3,000 U.S. troops will go to nearby countries to help arrange airlift for emergency supplies.
